Daniel to schedule technical deep-dive / infra review with Raj the week of 2025-03-24

summary: Discovery with First Harbor Bank to understand data residency, logging restrictions, and compliance requirements across Hosted / Dedicated / Private deployment options. Customer is evaluating Redwood for a customer-facing chat and document ingestion pipeline for risk and account servicing; primary concerns are GDPR, GLBA/HIPAA applicability for some products, strict log retention/no raw transcript logging, and proof of subprocessors/DPA. AE + SE covered high-level product modes, dedicated/private options, KMS/HSM and audit log capabilities, and proposed next steps: share SOC2/HIPAA docs, schedule tech deep dive for VPC/network, and provide Dedicated pricing.
topics: Overview of customer use cases (chat + doc ingestion)
HIPAA/financial controls applicability (GLBA) and logging restrictions
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
00:00 Maya Patel: All right good afternoon everyone this is Maya from Redwood, thanks for taking the time. we've got Daniel from our solutions team as well. can we do quick intros?
00:12 Sarah Lawson: Hi Sarah Lawson head of data governance at First Harbor. we're evaluating some LLM workflows for customer support and fraud detection, um also some doc ingestion for loan processing.
00:22 Raj Patel: Raj, cloud architect, I'll be doing the infra review.
00:25 Tom Nguyen: Tom, security and compliance. I'll flag any regs.
00:28 Emily Cho: Emily product, owner of the use case.
00:30 Maya Patel: Great thanks. quick agenda we want to cover use case, what regs you think apply, residency needs, and talk through our hosted/dedicated/private options and what controls each gives you, sound good?
00:40 Sarah Lawson: Yep, that's perfect. to jump in high level we have EU customers and US customers; EU data for EU customers should remain in EU per legal guidance. also certain doc types may be PII or even health data for small subset of products so need to understand HIPAA implications. financial data obviously GLBA concerns as well.
01:00 Daniel Kim: Got it. just to frame Redwood quickly: hosted API is our fastest path, Dedicated is reserved capacity with predictable throughput and isolation, and Private gives you a customer-managed control plane (VPC / on prem) for stricter network controls. you can pin versions and we support KMS integrations for key management.
01:20 Tom Nguyen: On the hosted option our main blocker is logs. we can't have raw customer transcripts stored outside the EU and we need strict retention windows. can we disable transcript logging entirely?
01:34 Daniel Kim: Yes there's a couple levers. by default we log requests for telemetry but we offer configs to redact or disable persistent transcript logs. with Dedicated you can choose not to persist logs to our hosted observability and instead ship them to your S3 in region or disable at all. with Private you control logs entirely. note that some orchestration and metrics may still need ephemeral telemetry for stability unless you opt into full air-gapped deployment.
01:58 Sarah Lawson: When you say "disable" are there still any retained ephemeral logs for debugging? legal wants zero long-term storage of raw unredacted transcripts.
02:08 Daniel Kim: You can configure to redact PII at ingestion and disable transcript capture. ephemeral traces for performance are held in memory and rotated but not written to disk if you choose. i'm gonna be careful with wording here because sometimes the auto-transcript says different things, but technically you can operate in a mode where no raw transcripts are persisted off-host.
02:28 Raj Patel: For us the network flow matters. with Dedicated, do you still have control plane calls that go to Redwood's control plane out of region? we need to ensure any control-plane metadata doesn't contain PII and ideally stays in-region.
02:42 Maya Patel: For Dedicated we offer a hybrid control plane model. control plane calls (billing, metadata) by default hit our control plane; we can sign a contract for in-region control plane for enterprise deals or you can choose Private which gives you a full customer-managed control plane in your V P C. we also have options to minimize metadata: strip meeting titles, redact request identifiers. we can surface a DPA and subprocessors list.
03:03 Tom Nguyen: subprocessors list is key. we need to know if any third parties see customer data, include cloud providers, logging vendors.
03:12 Maya Patel: We'll send our current subprocessors list and SOC2 report. note that in many Dedicated deals customers include an addendum that limits subprocessors or requires notification.
03:22 Emily Cho: Another angle is residency: EU data must remain in EU but some workflows will reach out to external APIs for enrichment - does Redwood support routing by policy per request?
03:34 Daniel Kim: Yes you can route by region and model policy. you can tag requests by customer region and route to EU-hosted capacity. we also support model fallbacks but fallbacks can be restricted to same region.
03:45 Sarah Lawson: For GDPR we also need DSAR handling and deletion. if a user requests deletion we need to ensure the raw data and embeddings are removed. how do you handle embedding stores and cache?
03:58 Daniel Kim: Embeddings and KV cache can be controlled. by default embeddings can be stored in region-backed stores; we can also set TTLs and provide APIs to purge keys. for Hosted customers we provide APIs to delete objects and we'll honor DSARs; for Dedicated and Private you have more direct control and can manage retention in your own stores.
04:20 Tom Nguyen: encryption stuff - KMS or HSM? we need CMEK and HSM-backed keys for some products.
04:28 Maya Patel: We support customer-managed keys via KMS for Dedicated and Private. HSM integrations are available for enterprise - most customers use cloud KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) and we can show key rotation and audit logs.
04:40 Raj Patel: Does the Hosted option allow CMEK?
04:43 Daniel Kim: Hosted can support CMEK for enterprise plans with a dedicated tenant, but typically Dedicated or Private are the recommended routes for strict key control.
04:51 Sarah Lawson: Ok timeline and success criteria: we need to prove residency, no raw transcript logs, DSAR purge, and evidence of SOC2 + HIPAA controls for data in transit and at rest. we also want a POC with a small dataset to run latency/cost numbers.
05:10 Maya Patel: That's a good checklist. for POC we usually do a week-long pilot on Dedicated or Hosted with EU-only capacity and run some benchmarks. Daniel can run a technical deep-dive with Raj to size capacity.
05:22 Daniel Kim: Yep i'll schedule the infra review. a few quick clarifying questions about your workloads - are you seeing long sequence docs or mostly short chats?
05:30 Emily Cho: For customer support it's short chats but document ingestion can be ~5-8k tokens per doc, sometimes larger.
05:36 Daniel Kim: Ok that matters for batching and kernel selection. for longer sequences we recommend models with better long-context support and we can run quantization profiles to reduce cost.
05:44 Tom Nguyen: On logging again - what about audit logs for access? we need immutable audit trails that show who accessed what and when, without exposing content.
05:54 Maya Patel: Our Console provides audit logs separate from transcript logs. audit records are metadata only (request id, user id, action, timestamp) and we can redact parameters. audit logs can be forwarded to your logging endpoint in-region. they are also tamper-evident via append-only storage options if required.
06:10 Raj Patel: Do you integrate with our SAML SSO and RBAC? we want fine-grained role control on who can pull transcripts.
06:18 Daniel Kim: Yes SSO via SAML and OIDC supported; RBAC is configurable with role templates and you can restrict export/download permissions.
06:24 Michael Ortiz: On legal - what about DPA and liability carve outs? we need a DPA that covers subprocessors, data transfers (standard contractual clauses, SCCs), and clear jurisdiction clauses.
06:36 Maya Patel: We have a standard DPA that includes SCC attachments for EU transfers and we can add custom clauses for enterprise. we'll share the DPA draft and our Data Processing Addendum link.
06:44 Sarah Lawson: About Schrems II, do you have guidance on SCCs and US access?
06:49 Maya Patel: We have legal guidance and our default approach for EU residency is to host EU customer data in EU regions, use SCCs, and limit access. for stricter needs Private deployment inside your VPC eliminates the cross-border risk.
07:02 Emily Cho: Can you clarify the tradeoff for latency vs cost between Hosted and Dedicated?
07:08 Daniel Kim: Hosted is typically more cost-effective for spiky workloads but Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower median latency due to reserved GPUs. cost per token is usually lower with Dedicated if you have steady usage.
07:20 Sarah Lawson: Are there limits on model variants in Dedicated?
07:24 Daniel Kim: You can run our curated models; for Dedicated we can also support specific weights and quantization profiles. some bleeding-edge builds may be available on Hosted sooner.
07:33 Tom Nguyen: Ok can you talk through an example network diagram for Dedicated + VPC peering?
07:37 Daniel Kim: Sure i'll share a diagram but in short: for Dedicated we provision a GPU pool in a cloud region; control plane calls can be proxied through a regional control plane; data plane traffic can be restricted to your VPC via peering or private link. if you want full isolation we suggest Private where the control plane also lives in your VPC and data never leaves your network.
07:56 Raj Patel: When you say "data plane traffic" is that for inference only or also for model pulls and updates?
08:03 Daniel Kim: Data plane is inference. model weights updates are managed and you can pin versions; model pulls for weights may require connectivity to our model registry unless you host weights yourself in Private.
08:15 Sarah Lawson: Are transcripts or embeddings ever used for training or model improvements?
08:21 Maya Patel: No - not by default. we can only use customer data for improvements with explicit opt-in. enterprise contracts typically prohibit usage for training and we include that language in the DPA.
08:33 Tom Nguyen: For auditability we need to capture request hashes without content. can you support content hashing to verify data was processed without storing the content?
08:44 Daniel Kim: Yes we can store content hashes and metadata only. that pattern is common for customers who need verifiable audit without retaining raw content.
08:52 Emily Cho: Any thought on redaction at the model layer vs client side?
08:56 Daniel Kim: We recommend client-side redaction for highest guarantee but server-side pre-processing can help with consistency. we can support both and surface libraries for redaction.
09:06 Maya Patel: i'd like to surface a couple of common objections - cost of Dedicated vs compliance need and complexity of Private. many banks start with Dedicated to get isolation and performance and then move to Private for strictest controls.
09:20 Sarah Lawson: Pricing will be a factor, yes. we need to present TCO to leadership.
09:24 Maya Patel: We'll include a cost model in the follow-up.
09:28 Raj Patel: For the POC can we get an example config that disables transcript logging, uses EU-only capacity, and ships audit logs to our S3?
09:36 Daniel Kim: Absolutely. i'll prepare a sample stack: Dedicated EU pool, VPC peering, CMEK with AWS KMS, no transcript persistence, audit logs to S3 + CloudTrail integration.
09:48 Tom Nguyen: And for legal can you provide HIPAA attestation and an example BAA? we have a small product that touches health-adjacent data.
09:56 Maya Patel: We have a HIPAA overview and BAA templates for enterprise customers. we'll include those docs. note, HIPAA applicability sometimes depends on whether you're a covered entity.
10:06 Sarah Lawson: Good point we'll loop legal on that.
10:09 Michael Ortiz: One other ask: our auditors want to see proof that subprocessors have SOC2 or equivalent. do you have that evidence?
10:17 Maya Patel: We can supply subprocessors with attestations and our SOC2 report. some subprocessors may have different attestations but we include that in the subprocessors list.
10:25 Emily Cho: timeline wise we want a technical deep-dive next week and legal to review DPA.
10:31 Maya Patel: Sounds good. i'll send the docs and propose times for the deep dive.
10:36 Sarah Lawson: Quick nit - can you confirm retention windows for embeddings if we set TTL 90 days? we need guaranteed deletion after that window.
10:45 Daniel Kim: We support TTL-forced deletion and will provide APIs and logs showing deletion events. for Dedicated you can enforce deletion in your store; we can also confirm via audit events.
10:54 Raj Patel: Ok last technical question - how do you handle backups and snapshots? if backups are stored cross-region that could violate residency.
11:03 Daniel Kim: Good call. we can configure backups to be region-scoped and disable cross-region replication. for Dedicated and Private it's something we include in the infra checklist.
11:15 Tom Nguyen: Thanks everyone - this was helpful.
11:18 Maya Patel: Recap: Maya will share SOC2, HIPAA, DPA draft, subprocessors list and pricing by 2025-03-20. Daniel will schedule tech deep dive with Raj and provide sample Dedicated stack. Customer will confirm residency list and legal contacts by 2025-03-25.
11:36 Sarah Lawson: Thanks we'll look for the materials.
11:40 Maya Patel: Thanks all talk soon.
11:45 [call ends]
